subject: SLA coverage optimization and pricing concessions
messages:
From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@brightline.ai>
To: mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-26 09:21:00 -0700
Subject: SLA options for Brightline production cutover

Hi Mateo,

Thanks again for the demo earlier this week. Brightline is preparing for a staged cutover in late Q3 and procurement asked me to get concrete SLA and pricing options so we can lock the vendor shortlist for the September 2nd review. A few constraints from legal/procurement: 1) we need an uptime SLA with clear credits, 2) defined response windows for Sev1/Sev2, 3) a named escalation path and weekly postmortem cadence for Sev1s, and 4) an option that includes cross-region failover (we're in us-west primary, eu-west DR).

Can you send 2–3 packaging options (one aggressive discount for longer term commit, one middle-of-the-road, and one minimal SLA) and indicate where we can trade latency/availability for price? Also let us know what you consider non-negotiable from an operational/contract standpoint.

Procurement timeline: vendor shortlist confirmed 2026-09-02, contract close targeted 2026-09-20.

Thanks,
Laura
---
Laura Chen
Head of Vendor Management | Brightline AI
laura.chen@brightline.ai

From: mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>

Cc: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-26 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA options for Brightline production cutover

Laura — thanks, appreciate the clear timeline. Attaching a short proposal that maps three pragmatic SLA/price profiles and the key operational tradeoffs (high level below). Attaching SLA_Pack_Proposal_v3.pdf with line-item credits.

Quick summary of the three packs:
- Core: 99.9% uptime, business-hours triage (M-F 08:00-18:00 PT), 8-hour Sev1 response, standard escalation path. Baseline price, low minimum commit. Good for dev/staging and low-risk production.
- Assured: 99.95% uptime, 24x7 triage, 2-hour Sev1 initial response + on-call continuous escalation, weekly Sev1 sync for 3 months after major incidents. ~15% uplift vs Core with a 12-month commit. Includes basic cross-region failover (manual warm standby).
- Premium: 99.99% uptime, 24x7 dedicated on-call, 30-min Sev1 response, named escalation (director-level) and automated cross-region failover with health-checked routing. ~35% uplift vs Core; requires a 12–24 month committed spend to qualify for the discount band.

Tradeoffs (where price sensitivity is highest):
- Availability banding: moving from 99.99 -> 99.95 yields the largest unit-cost reduction because it avoids the need for fully redundant warm pools and automated routing.
- On-call model: reducing from dedicated to shared on-call or business-hours coverage is a straightforward discount lever.
- Failover: automated cross-region failover is materially more expensive due to extra reserved capacity and routing orchestration; manual warm standby is cheaper but has longer RTO.

Non-negotiables from our side: security/compliance SLAs (audit log retention, controls for data residency) need to be in place; we also require a minimum notice period for major version rollouts that could affect inference outputs. Everything else we can place in tiered credits and escalation SLAs.

Vanessa/Ben — added you for pricing confirmation and to flag service credit thresholds. Laura, I'll follow up with a revised quote if you indicate which pack you prefer and any acceptable tradeoffs.

Best,
Mateo
Mateo Alvarez | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai | +1 (510) 555-0199

From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: mateo_alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>, Laura Chen <laura.chen@brightline.ai>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-26 14:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA options for Brightline production cutover

Laura / Mateo — quick pricing note to make the offer concrete. I've attached a pricing_breakdown_brightline.xlsx with line items and the commit tiers. Highlights:
- Core: $12k/month (no commit), credits prorated: 5% credit for monthly downtime > 99.9%
- Assured (recommended): $14k/month with a 12-month commit at list, or $11.9k/month with a 12-month prepay (10% prepay discount). Credits escalate per band (2% @ 99.9–99.94, 5% @ 99.85–99.89, 10% <99.85).
- Premium: $16.2k/month base with automated failover and director-level escalation; we can reach $13.5k/month with a 24-month commit + upfront purchase (roughly 17% effective discount).

Two additional options we can use to bridge the gap if procurement pushes back:
1) Response time swap: offer Assured uptime (99.95) with a 4-hour continuous incident window for a 7% price reduction vs 2-hour model.
2) Regional failover add-on: include manual warm standby (lower cost) as default and offer automated failover as a paid add-on that can be turned on during high-traffic windows.

I'd recommend Assured + 12-month prepay as a practical middle ground for production with cost visibility. Ben, can you confirm whether we can commit to the 10% prepay discount in the quote and include the failover add-on SKU?

Regards,
Vanessa Ortiz | Head of Commercial Ops, Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai

Attachment: pricing_breakdown_brightline.xlsx
From: Amir Shah <amir.shah@brightline.ai>
To: mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai
Cc: Laura Chen <laura.chen@brightline.ai>, vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-27 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA options for Brightline production cutover

Thanks — this is helpful. A couple of follow-ups before we present to procurement: we can likely land on Assured with the 12-month prepay, but procurement has two asks they say are must-haves to approve a mid-band commit category:

1) Include automated cross-region failover in the Assured package for the first 90 days after cutover (so we can do an initial soak with automated switching). After 90 days, convert to manual warm standby unless we elect to keep automated failover as an add-on.
2) A one-time onboarding credit equal to one month of service if Brightline signs by 2026-09-10 (procurement incentive).

Quote-back: we like the suggested response-time swap idea but would prefer the 4-hour continuous window if that gets us into the higher discount band.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept the 90-day automated failover temporary inclusion and the onboarding credit (or propose an alternative concession)?
